messages:
liz (support): FYI Velocore just opened a ticket — p95 tail latency jumped ~3x after yesterday's model roll (2026-03-12). Customer is on Dedicated, impact = user-facing timeouts. Ticket #V-4123.
chloe (sales): Customer report: p50 looks fine, p95 and error rate up when seq > ~1500 tokens. They're hitting penalties. :grimacing:
tom (eng-ml): Can you drop logs + request IDs? Is this only on large seqs or also short ones?
liz (support): pasted sample request ids: rID:0a7..., rID:0b9... — attached stack snippet in ticket. short summary: p50=180ms, p95 jumped from 420ms -> 1.2s for those requests.
ana (eng-runtime): @tom can you check KV cache hit rate and model variant fallbacks? We pushed a quantized variant yesterday, runtime may be routing to fallback for long seqs.
ana (eng-runtime): deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-12T22:04 by ana - model/velocore-v2-quantized
deploy-bot: ✅ canary passed
tom (eng-ml): quick profiler from customer's pod:
```
seq_len | p50 | p95
<512   | 160ms | 380ms
512-1500 | 220ms | 450ms
>1500  | 480ms | 1.25s
```
tom (eng-ml): KV cache hit rate drops to ~30% for >1500 sequences. Batching latency also increases (batch windows expand). Might be cache cold-start + model kernel path for long context.
ana (eng-runtime): Also seeing more small batches (1-2) on that workload; likely triggered by tokenization differences causing request splitting. Could be prompt prefix growth.
mike (product): Thanks. This is customer-impacting for Dedicated SLA customers. Need to decide scope: hotfix (rollback quantized variant / tweak routing) vs deeper change (batching improvements + cache warmup). What are acceptance criteria for shipping a fix? :clipboard:
tom (eng-ml): For hotfix: rollback to velocore-v2-emu (previous model) and monitor p95 back to baseline. Criteria: reproduce on Dedicated test cluster, p95 <= 500ms for >1500 seq, KV hit rate >70% after warmup.
ana (eng-runtime): For longer-term: add invariant tests for seq length distribution, add KV warmup after model swap, and routing policy change to avoid fallback on dedicated customers.
chloe (sales): Customer asks for rollback ASAP; they can tolerate a short outage window but want guarantee before EOD their time (UTC-5).
mike (product): Proposed plan: 1) Priority P1 for Dedicated customers. 2) Immediate rollback canary today if eng OK. 3) If rollback not acceptable, release routing tweak + patch to cache warming. 4) Product to open backlog item with launch criteria and QA testcases. 5) Communicate ETA to customer.
liz (support): I'll update ticket and set expectation. Customer asked for timeframe: ETA for rollback?
tom (eng-ml): Can do canary rollback in ~45min, full rollback + verification ~2h. Need oncall assist for verification.
ana (eng-runtime): I'll prepare metrics dashboard and a quick canary-runbook. cc @deploy-bot to schedule rollback when we say go.
deploy-bot: rollback scheduled for canary group when approved by @ana and @tom
mike (product): I'll create the backlog ticket with acceptance criteria: reproduction steps, perf thresholds, regression test (load/profile), docs update, and sign-off from eng-runtime. Also log customer comms.
chloe (sales): Please tag me in backlog ticket (chloe@redwood). Customer rep: Nora.
liz (support): Updating ticket #V-4123: plan = rollback canary -> monitor -> escalate if persists. ETA communicated.
tom (eng-ml): After rollback we'll also snapshot metrics to compare. If rollback fixes, we schedule deeper fix next sprint. If not, escalate to infra.
mike (product): scheduling 30m to sync now that we have plan. If anyone can't make, post updates in thread. :calendar:
ana (eng-runtime): adding runbook link to ticket and dashboard link in thread.
liz (support): Thanks all. I'll ping again once rollback starts. :thumbsup:
